post.description:
Sets the `zf_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax). An unknown e-mail, a wrong
password and a locked account all give the same 401. Five failures in a row lock the
account for a growing time, up to 15 minutes.

failure is the same 401, and clears the `zf_oidc_state` cookie.

get.summary:
Watches the workspace's events as they are decided: one `item` frame per outcome
(`accepted`, `flagged`, `unplanned`, `rejected` or `duplicate`), live only, with no
history. The stream resumes from the `Last-Event-ID` header, the `seq` of the last frame
seen, if the feed still holds the rows after it. A viewer that cannot keep up gets an
`event: gap` frame with the number of rows skipped (an upper bound when filters apply).
get.description:
While at least one viewer watches a workspace, ingestion writes a feed row per event;
when none does, it writes nothing extra. Values are masked per viewer as in the person
timeline; `reveal=true` shows the stored (redacted) values to a viewer who may see values
(owner, workspace admin or `admin` key) and is ignored for anyone else.

parameters.name: reveal
parameters.description: Show stored values to a viewer who may see values; default false

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The `id` of the last frame received

404.description: No such workspace, or no access to it

post.summary:
Uploads a CSV file as a new import. The body is the raw `text/csv` file, streamed into the
database in 1 MiB chunks; it must be UTF-8 (a byte order mark is ignored) with a header row
of unique names. The delimiter is detected from `,`, `;` and tab unless one is given. The
answer holds the import, its header and the first 20 rows, masked for callers who may not
see values. The import exists as `uploading` (hidden from the history) while the body
arrives, each 1 MiB chunk is stored on its own, and an upload that is refused, breaks off
or stalls for 60 seconds is deleted with its chunks. Audited as `import.created`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A name for the import, 1 to 128 characters

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: The file's name; defaults to name

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The source records are written under: a-z, 0-9, _ and -; default csv

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: The stream records are written under; default the file name without its extension

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.description: comma, semicolon or tab; detected when absent

201.description: The new import with its header and sample rows

400.description: A malformed query, or an upload that broke off

403.description: A key without the write scope, or a missing CSRF token

404.description: No such workspace, or no access to it

408.description: No byte arrived for 60 seconds; the upload was abandoned and nothing was kept

415.description: The content type is not text/csv

422.description: Not UTF-8, empty, or a header with blank or repeated names

post.summary:
Starts the dry run: maps every row of the file and keeps only the rejects (phase
`dry_run`) and the counters; no person, list or trait is written. The answer is the import
in `dry_running`; poll it until `dry_run_done`. Needs a saved mapping.

Saves the mapping and moves the import to `mapped`. The mapping needs at least one
identifier target, columns the file has, and trait keys that exist and are not archived;
list targets must exist. Allowed until the first run starts; saving clears the counters and
rejects of an earlier dry run.

403.description: A key without the write scope, or a missing CSRF token

409.description: The import is running or has ended

422.description: The mapping is invalid; the detail names the rule and the column

get.summary:

get.summary:
The rejects as a CSV, `row_number,column,reason` with one line per problem, streamed page
by page. For the owner, workspace admins and `admin` keys the rows' own cells follow, under
the file's column names; cells that start like a spreadsheet formula get a leading quote.
Everyone else with read access gets the codes alone. Audited as `import.rejects_downloaded`.

400.description: A malformed phase

403.description: A key without the read scope

404.description: No such workspace or import, or no access

post.summary:
Starts the run: applies every row in batches of 500, each batch one transaction that
writes the profile records, adds the list members, keeps the rejects and advances the
checkpoint. A crash resumes from the checkpoint. The run fails with `reject_threshold` once
more than 1,000 rows are done and the rejected share is above the import's threshold; the
batches already applied stay applied. Running the same file again with the same source and
stream changes nothing. The answer is the import in `running`; poll it. Audited as
`import.run_started`.

403.description: A key without the write scope, or a missing CSRF token

404.description: No such workspace or import, or no access

409.description: The import has no mapping, is busy, or has ended

post.summary:
Replays rejected events after a schema or policy fix. With `dry_run` it validates each
reject's stored, redacted payload against the current schema and policy and predicts the
outcome, writing nothing. Without it, a job stores each event that now passes, once, with
the flag `replayed` (and `no_triggers` unless `emit_triggers`), sets `replayed_at` and
`replay_event_id` on the reject and records an `event.replayed` decision with the cause.
Replaying a reject again changes nothing. A reject that named no person cannot be
replayed (`still_rejected` with `no_person`).

404.description: No such workspace, or no access to it

get.summary:
Everything the system holds about one person: identities grouped by the sources that list
them, traits with the source and time of each value, consent, lists and the people merged

workspace admins and `admin` keys, and masked for everyone else.

consent, list memberships and their history, conflicts, merges and decisions. It adds no
suppression and no erasure ledger entry; use an erasure request for a data-subject request.
Needs the workspace admin role and the CSRF token. Audited as `person.deleted`.

post.summary:
Asks for a person to be erased: the ledger keeps the person id and the keyed hashes of
their identifiers, the email and phone stay suppressed as `erased`, and the person and
everything that refers to them is deleted by a background job. The request is given as a
`person_id` or as an `identifier`; one that resolves to no person is a 404. Needs the
workspace admin role and the CSRF token. Audited as `privacy.erasure_requested`.

202.description: The request, pending until the job has run

403.description: Not a workspace admin, a key without the admin scope, or a missing CSRF token

404.description: No such workspace or person, or no access

422.description: The body names both or neither of person_id and identifier, or the identifier is malformed

post.summary:
Asks for an export of everything held about a person: profile, identities, ledger
contributions, events, consent and its history, lists and their history, merges and
